item_title: AT 15:00 ET — Bessent's Iran package landed, and its sharpest edge is aimed at China rather than at Iran
mechanism: Sanctioning oil that has already stopped moving shifts the binding instrument from the barrel to the payment rail, so the exposure moves to Chinese refiners and the banks that clear their trade.

scenarios.direction: The effect shows up in trade finance, shipping insurance and correspondent-banking withdrawal in the third countries named, while crude stays soft.
scenarios.why: This is the falsifiable form of the claim: it predicts the compliance layer moves, not the commodity. If oil rallies on enforcement instead, the reading is wrong.
scenarios.precedent: Today ran the test once already — the package landed and WTI fell about 2.5% to $84.89 rather than rising, and Iran's own loadings are down to roughly 287,000 barrels a day from about 2 million pre-war. There is very little barrel left to sanction.

scenarios.direction: China treats the dollar-system threat as the escalation it is and answers elsewhere, making this a US-China dispute that outlives the Iran file.
scenarios.why: Naming a G2 counterparty as not exempt, over a trade it conducts at 90% of the exporter's volume, is a different act from designating shadow-fleet tankers.
scenarios.precedent: The map already carries an active US-China escalation channel on the technology side — the Taiwan Nvidia-server smuggling indictments and China's 2026-2030 cyber-industry plan, both on the 08-23 page. A second channel opening on the financial side is the thing to watch for.

context_note: capital-context's conflict_risk_premium reading has tracked oil falling while rhetoric escalates for weeks, and today is its strongest instance, because the escalation was the enforcement itself.

item_title: SoftBank's record ¥1tn retail bond gets its terms — and a reason it had to be retail
mechanism: When the institutional bid for an AI-linked borrower thins, funding re-routes to retail at a higher coupon instead of stopping — and that re-routing prices the risk banks declined to hold.

scenarios.direction: Prices at or above the top of the 4.3-4.9% range on 09-04, and later AI-linked Japanese issuance keeps leaning on retail rather than institutional books.
scenarios.why: The falsifiable form: the funding channel stays shifted, not just that one deal was dear. A below-range print would mean retail demand was strong, not institutions absent.
scenarios.precedent: SoftBank's own April 2025 Y600bn retail bond — the prior Japanese record, same instrument used the same way — makes this deal measurable against a known coupon rather than a hypothetical.

scenarios.direction: It clears inside the range, and bank reluctance proves to be about SoftBank's leverage and Arm concentration, not AI credit generally.
scenarios.why: SoftBank is an unusually leveraged borrower with a stalled-loan history this map tracks. Reluctance toward SoftBank is not reluctance toward the buildout; conflating them is the error here.
scenarios.precedent: The 2026-08-06 Q1 FY26 print — profit down 18%, Arm's slide erasing Y14T of pro-forma NAV — is already on Son All-In as an issuer-specific shock with no read-across to peers.

context_note: Sits against the standing picture's AI-credit strand and Circular Financing, which has run on argument rather than a printed price. 09-04 supplies the number.

item_title: Texas's attorney general runs against data centers, and puts the sales-tax exemption on the block
mechanism: Opposition reaches project economics through the subsidy line, not the moratorium line: campaigning to repeal a sales-tax exemption turns backlash into a cash-flow variable lenders can discount.

scenarios.direction: The exemption's status appears as a named sensitivity in Texas data-center financings, S-1 risk factors or rating commentary, whether or not Paxton wins.
scenarios.why: That is what this thread was opened to detect: the first lender or prospectus explicitly discounting for backlash. A campaign plank is upstream; the test is propagation into pricing.
scenarios.precedent: Anthropic's coming S-1 was reported 2026-08-21 to name data-center opposition as a risk factor — the same propagation one step earlier, already on this thread's record.

scenarios.direction: It stays rhetoric, the exemption survives the legislative session, and the episode reads as a primary-season position with no financing consequence.
scenarios.why: Repeal needs the Texas legislature, not an attorney general, and the state's revenue interest cuts the other way. The plank signals where politics is moving, not an enacted instrument.
scenarios.precedent: Abbott's 08-03 pause on new data centers pending the ERCOT/PUCT audit is the near-comparator whose financing effect is so far nil — announced, real, not visible in any priced instrument.

context_note: Datacenter Sites tracks the siting fights; this thread tracks whether they become a priced line item. The tax-exemption clause is what puts Paxton in the second category.
